extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, suitable for reinforcement leaming of SWE agents at scale.
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A scalable, fully automated pipeline for continuous collection of software engineering tasks from real-world GitHub repositories.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Issues are linked with pull requests that mention resolving them, applying filters to select instances where the issue is from a Python repository with a permissive license, marked as resolved, merged into the main branch, and affects 1 to 15 files.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: An instruction-following model was fine-tuned using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset uses an automated pipeline for a continuous supply of fresh tasks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark may accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering, bringing potential risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The initial release is limited exclusively to Python, restricting its immediate applicability to other language ecosystems.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement leaming-based approaches.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: we present a scalable, fully automated pipeline for continuous collection of software engineering tasks from real-world GitHub repositories.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive [Grigorik, 2011] and GitHub.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive [Grigorik, 2011] and GitHub.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: To initiate the dataset building process, we download approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We then link issues with pull requests that mention resolving them in their title or description, applying filters to select instances where: The issue is from a Python repository with a permissive license. The issue is marked as resolved. The PR is merged into the main branch... Changes affect 1 to 15 files.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: To assess these properties automatically, we fine-tune an instruction-following model using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict: Issue Clarity... Task Complexity... Test Patch Correctness.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We fine-tune Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct using annotations from SWE-bench Verified.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: SWE-rebench uses an automated pipeline from Section 2 for a continuous supply of fresh tasks.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Finally, while our benchmark is intended to support transparency and standardization in evaluating SWE agents, it may also accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering. This progress brings potential risks, such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The initial release of SWE-rebench is limited exclusively to Python, restricting its immediate applicability to other language ecosystems.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement leaming-based approaches.
